questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
I had the impression that the students were better in their practical skills than we were taught back home. And because it was another Nordic country did I aspect their English level to be around the same as my own. 
Other than that, I found it interesting to go to Finland because it is not a typical travel destination, and I would probably not have visited the country if it wasn't for an exchange.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
The language was a big obstacle in my learning. And because either a student or a teacher didn't speak/ didn't want to speak English in the group most of the teaching would be in Finnish. Some teachers were better at staying in English, but a lot was really bad. Also, when there was a procedure that did not happened all the time, like a urine catheter, we would never get the opportunity to try (Other than in Saari) because the teacher would only ask in Finnish or the students would already have picked someone to do it without asking. 
Some departments were good, but it really depended on the students and the vet that was there. 
The Winter in Helsinki it though because people are very closed off and there are not a lot of social activities. But the spring is nicer, and people open more up, and it becomes easier to do outside activities  
I would recommend going here if you are interested in farm animals because you get to do a lot of practical work in Saari (the production animal hospital) and visit actual farms like in a normal practice. The problem here is that you must rely on the Finnish students to give you a ride because you can't go there with public transportation. And that some of the teachers here don't really speak English so you can't choose which teachers you would like to go on farm visits with, so sometimes you can end up looking at horses all day when you wanted to look at cattle.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
It was pretty easy. We had a really nice contact person, Eeva, who had already given us a lot of information before arriving and I also wrote and asked her a lot of questions before we arrived. We also got some tutors, but they were not a lot of help. 
On our first day there we got to meet the other exchange students, got the rest of the information we needed from Eeva and got a tour of the hospital which was nice and got pointed out which department we should be in the next day.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had the introduction day with Eeva but that was basically that. I know it was written in the schedule which weeks there were exchange students in the departments, but the vets didn't seem to know so there was no introduction on our first real day at the hospital.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
We had two options when we applied for housing: UNIHOME or HOAS. 
I chose UNIHOME. 
It is not possible to ask for a specific housing type or address in either Unihome or HOAS. All the veterinarians who applied through unihome got a room at Vuolukiventie in Pihlajamäki which is in walking distance from Viikki campus. The veterinarians who lived in HOAS had to take public transportation, but it was easy to get to campus.   
-	HOAS: Here you will always get one or more roommates. You will have a shared kitchen and bathroom. 
-	UNIHOME: I applied through unihome because they had more rooms in general. But my wish was to live in a dorm. All exchange students in 2022 applied for a room at a dorm but we all got apartments. In the apartment you have your own bathroom and kitchen but no oven. When we arrived, most people had already been there for over a month, so the social life was not really shared in the group.      
If you arrive here, we will recommend you wait buying applies for the kitchen because there is often some leftover stuff from other exchanges students in the reception.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: There is no on campus living in Helsinki, so this is the only option. When I arrived in February, most people had already been there for over a month, so the social life was not really shared in the group. There was a Whatsapp group, but I would recommend coming sooner or in the spring if it is possible

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The room was nice enough but there was a leak from my bathroom, so the floor was damaged when I moved in. Otherwise, the room was furnished and there was enough room to have friends over. There was nothing left in the apartment so I had to buy all the things I needed for my kitchen and stuff, but it was okay.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I applied for a mixed rotation with focus on small animals. I later got a schedule from Eeva with a week-to-week program only in the small animal hospital. But it was very easy to change the schedule in the beginning and I ended up with two weeks in the production animal hospital as well.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I mainly used Eeva and she was really nice and quick to answer. I think you could also have asked some of the tutors.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I only applied for the rotation and not for any courses so it was succesful

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It was easy to change weeks in the hospital before arrival but afterwards when you had started it was almost impossible to change between the departments because there were too many students in the departments I wanted to be in as well

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
The language barrier was a big problem and closed off groups of either students or a vet or a nurse that didn't include me limited the learning I had. There were a lot of discussions on case-based patients but they were almost all in Finnish so we couldn't participate.
Some teachers let us have our own patients and do as much as possible by our self, but some wouldn't let us do anything. 
I would like to point out that I had really good weeks with a lot of learning in Surgery (here especially with Nina), Internal Medicine (here especially with Susanna and the vets Noora and Julia) and in the special departments with Dermatology, Exotics, Ophthalmology and Dentistry.   
In experience is that the Finnish students are not challenged a lot in their academical learning in a lot of the departments but more told what to do. On the other hand, they are then good with practical learning and lets the students do a lot of the work which is nice.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I only had practical learning in the small animal hospital and in the production animal hospital. There were no lectures and no exam but just practical day to day learning.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
Hands on:
Even though I didn't have as much hands on learning as the Finnish students I still got to do more then I would have back home. It is nice that the students gets to try a lot of stuff so it isn't the first time trying it in practice life. I improved skills like ultrasound, placing an iv-catheter and surgical skills.  
Time:
The tempo in the hospital was very slow which could be frustrating but also gave you a lot of time to try technics and to be able to finish the paperwork and not be stressed which was nice.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: I did the rotation where I was in these departments: small animal general polyclinics, diagnostic imaging, small animal internal medicine, on-call duty, small animal hospital special clinics; dermatology, cardiology and exotics and neurology, ophthalmology and dentistry, anesthesia small animal, surgery small animals and in the production animal hospital.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend doing weeks in small animal internal medicine, small animal hospital special clinics; dermatology, cardiology and exotics and neurology, ophthalmology and dentistry, anesthesia small animal, surgery small animals and the production animal hospital.  
Anesthesia can be a little hard because there is a lot of people, and it can be a little stressful so they can quickly switch to Finnish. In diagnostic the teachers in ultrasound are really good at explaining in English but it is the nurses what takes the pictures in x-ray, and they don't really speak English, so it is hard to learn anything in there. They also have an MRI and CT machine, but the students are not really allowed in there.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Having to buy supplies for the apartment. Even though I brought as much as possible in reuse, I still spend 80 EUR.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries, alcohol and going out to eat was really expensive and so was going out to a bar. Public transportation was cheaper than I had expected and was easily accessible.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I found it hard to find information about this. They have a student organization HYY but their website is really confusing and their opening hour were always when I was at the hospital

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: We had our social tutor who introduced us to some events but often quite late. We had one international dinner with the tutors but other than that there was nothing planned for us. I followed ESNunihelsinki for information about international event and were told by other students which event I could come to

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go to some of the events planned by ESN to meet other exchange students, make friends with the Finnish students so they can tell you about the events that are happening. But Vappu (the 1th of May) is a really big thing in Finland and you should definitely be in Helsinki for the parties in the streets surrounding that day.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Experiences in Helsinki:
All the touristy stuff you can easily do in the city: 
o	Café Regatte: both in wintertime where you can walk on the ocean but also when the ice is melted, and you can just enjoy the beautiful view. Recommended at sunset 
o	The Cathedrals: Both the white and the Russian. 
o	The libraries: the national library of Finland and Oodi
o	Old market square 
o	Temppeliaukio Rock Church 
o	Helsinki Zoo 
o	Esplanade Park with Havest Amanda 
o	Suomenlinnia
o	National Museum of Helsinki
o	Löyly sauna 
o	Sompa sauna – Free and a lot of locals here. Be prepared for a lot of nudity and a true Finnish experience.  

Outside Helsinki:
o	Turku: one- or two-day trip 
o	Porvoo: half to one day trip 
o	Tampere: one day trip
o	Tallin, Estonia: two day trip 
o	Lapland: didn't manage to go myself but would definitely recommend it. 3 to 5 days   
-	When the snow has melted/Hiking:
o	Kuusijärvi/ Sipoonkorpi National Park: Not that far from Viikki. Have a very nice sauna as well 
o	Central Park 
o	Roihuvuori Cherry Park – Kirsiklapuisto: for the cherry blossom 
o	Lammassaari 
o	Kaisaniemi Botanic Garden
o	Walk in the districts: Töölö (and around the lake), Torikorttelit, Kruununhaka, Katajanokka, Kallio and Eira    
o	Nuuksio National Park: A bit of a journey from Helsinki but definitely wroth it. You can also sleep in the forest. 

Places to eat:
-	Fat Raman: the one in Kallio 
-	Hills Dumplings 
-	Teurastamo 
-	Lie Mi 
-	The market hall 
-	Somewhere where you can get a good salmon soup ;)

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I would recommend trying to learn some Finnish before going there. Even though I only spoke very little it helped me a bit in my day-to-day life because a lot of the people there only speaks Finnish. Otherwise, the culture is much like the Danish, but the Finnish people are more introvert and can be hard to get to know.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
I started talking with the students about other stuff than academical learning, so they would relax more in speaking English. A lot of them are introverts so they will often not start a conversation with you by them self. So don't be afraid to speak to them and I always wrote to the students I like and asked them if they wanted to do something outside the hospital and they always wanted to.  
Also just being honest and not speaking about superficial stuff helped getting true friends

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Definitely the language barrier. The Finns are often not bad in English, but they are very unsure about speaking English and because a lot of them are not that outgoing, it can be hard to get friend.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Vappu and going to the market square after winning the world championship in ice hockey. Also just in general being outside in the nature. It is very easy to find a green area anywhere and I loved that.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be prepared for the language barrier. Maybe it was worse for me because of covid but it was really hard getting people to speak English and staying in English. I would say you have to be pretty persistent and not shy to feel comfortable in this. 
I recommend you download google translate to you phone, so you can translate the journals in that way. Otherwise use the computers on campus and the translations app “Deepl” to understand the journals. You can also ask to get access to “provet” from home, so you have time to prepare from home. 
Find the tutor in the group. In almost every group of students there is a tutor, so that person can help you understand what is going on if there is something you don't understand or need help with. 
Don't be afraid to speak your mind. If there is a lot of Finnish or you don't feel included in the group start talking with the students about it. If this feels over your boundaries you can always talk with the exchange coordinator Eeva. I did this a lot and it really helped. 
Try to become friends with the Finnish students. They can be hard to get to know in the beginning but once you have them as friends everything becomes much easier.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I think I got most of it down here but if you have any more questions, you are welcome to contact me.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
Getting to be part of true Finnish experiences and not just feeling like a tourist. It was easier for me to get invited to these events because I prioritized being with the Finnish students. 
Also improving my practical skills both in small animals and in large.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The language and feeling like I had to proof myself all the time.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
